title.es: Persuadir y dar consejos con tacto

objective: Al terminar convences a alguien con argumentos y estrategias lingüísticas: sugerencias, advertencias, ejemplos y cierre firme pero cortés.

warmup.prompt_es: Convencer no es insistir: es ofrecer razones, anticipar objeciones y dejar la puerta abierta. En inglés hay recursos muy concretos para persuadir sin presionar.

lines.speaker: Marta
lines.text: Have you thought about joining the yoga class at the community centre? It's only ten euros a month.
lines.es: ¿Has pensado en apuntarte a la clase de yoga del centro cívico? Son solo diez euros al mes.

lines.speaker: Jon
lines.text: I'm not sure. I'm not flexible at all, and I'd probably feel out of place.
lines.es: No sé. No soy nada flexible y seguramente me sentiría fuera de lugar.

lines.speaker: Marta
lines.text: That's exactly what I thought at first! But the teacher is great with beginners. Besides, you don't need to be flexible to start: that's what the classes are for.
lines.es: ¡Eso mismo pensé yo al principio! Pero la profesora es genial con los principiantes. Además, no necesitas ser flexible para empezar: para eso son las clases.

lines.speaker: Jon
lines.text: Hmm. I'd have to find the time, though. My schedule is packed.
lines.es: Mmm. Tendría que encontrar tiempo. Mi agenda está llena.

lines.speaker: Marta
lines.text: Think about it this way: if you spent just one hour a week on it, you'd feel less stressed and sleep better. Isn't that worth an hour?
lines.es: Míralo así: si dedicaras solo una hora a la semana, estarías menos estresado y dormirías mejor. ¿No vale la pena una hora?

lines.speaker: Jon
lines.text: When you put it like that... Is there a trial class?
lines.es: Dicho así... ¿Hay una clase de prueba?

lines.speaker: Marta
lines.text: Yes, the first one is free. What have you got to lose? And I'll come with you, if that helps.
lines.es: Sí, la primera es gratis. ¿Qué tienes que perder? Y yo iré contigo, si eso ayuda.

lines.speaker: Jon
lines.text: All right, you've convinced me. But if I hate it, I'm not going back!
lines.es: Vale, me has convencido. ¡Pero si lo odio, no vuelvo!

lines.speaker: Marta
lines.text: Deal. Honestly, I think you'll be pleasantly surprised.
lines.es: Trato hecho. Sinceramente, creo que te llevarás una agradable sorpresa.

glossary.lemma: what have you got to lose
glossary.example: What have you got to lose?

md_es: **Frases para persuadir con cortesía**
| Estrategia | Frases |
| **Sugerir** | *Have you thought about + -ing? · Why don't you …? · How about + -ing? · You might want to …* |
| **Anticipar objeciones** | *I know what you're thinking, but … · I thought the same at first, but …* |
| **Dar razones** | *Besides, … · On top of that, … · What's more, … · The point is …* |
| **Reformular** | *Think about it this way: … · Look at it from another angle: …* |
| **Beneficios** | *You'd feel … · It would help you … · You'll be surprised how …* |
| **Reducir el riesgo** | *What have you got to lose? · The first one is free. · You can always stop if you don't like it.* |
| **Ofrecer ayuda** | *I'll come with you. · I can help you get started.* |
| **Cerrar** | *Why not give it a try? · Shall we sign you up? · Promise me you'll think about it.* |
**Condicional para persuadir**
- *If you spent just an hour a week, you'd feel better.* (segundo condicional: hipótesis atractiva)
- *If you don't try, you'll never know.* (primer condicional: advertencia suave)
- *You'd be surprised how …* · *You'll thank me later.*
**Convencer vs obligar**
- *persuade / convince someone to do something*: *She persuaded me to join.* ✘ *persuaded me join*.
- *convince someone that …*: *I convinced him that it was safe.*
- *talk someone into + -ing*: *He talked me into buying it.* · *talk someone out of + -ing*: *She talked me out of leaving.*
**Responder con tacto cuando no estás convencido**
- *I'll think about it. · I see your point, but … · That's tempting, but … · Let me sleep on it.*
**Errores típicos**
- ✘ *You must to try.* → ✔ *You should try it.* / *You really should try it.*
- ✘ *I convinced him to that it was safe.* → ✔ *I convinced him that it was safe.*
- ✘ *Why you don't come?* → ✔ *Why don't you come?*
- ✘ *How about to go?* → ✔ *How about going?*

**Ojo:** *besides* (además) ≠ *beside* (al lado de). *Persuade* y *convince* son casi sinónimos, pero *convince* se centra en la creencia y *persuade* en la acción. *Advice* (consejo) incontable; *advise* (verbo).
Pronunciación: *persuade* /pəˈsweɪd/ · *convince* /kənˈvɪns/ · *besides* /bɪˈsaɪdz/.
